title: Implement Rio v0.1 local review CLI
body:
Rio currently contains the v0.1 planning artifacts. This implements the local review CLI and completes all 66 tasks in `rio-v0-1-local-cli`.

### Changes

- Add the Rust workspace, `rio review`, `rio doctor`, profile commands, configuration, schemas, and built-in modules.
- Implement exact Git snapshots, pure shared source caches, per-worktree dependency links in disposable tool trees, and supervised tool execution with timeout, cancellation, output limits, and descendant cleanup.
- Add TypeScript/Python diagnostics, coverage, dependency compatibility and OSV auditing, secret checks, impact graphs, finding identity/state classification, and text/Markdown/JSON reports.
- Add cross-platform CI, Unix/PowerShell installers, six-target release builds, provenance attestations, verified draft publication and recovery, documentation, benchmarks, and automated acceptance evidence.

### Validation

- [Green CI](https://github.com/mctlisboa/rio-v01-validation-20261104/actions/runs/41918738887) on Ubuntu, macOS ARM64, and Windows. The workspace suite passed 164 Rust tests with zero ignored tests; fixture suites, required-tool checks, process supervision, and installers passed. Removing Ruff correctly fails the required-tool check. Windows installers passed in PowerShell 5.1 and 7.
- [RC release validation](https://github.com/mctlisboa/rio-v01-validation-20261104/actions/runs/41916670430): all six target builds and installer smokes passed; the published prerelease has six archives, six verified provenance bundles, checksums, and both installers. Forced upload failure left only a draft; the recovery run replaced it, verified every asset, and published without changing `releases/latest`.
- [Published installer validation](https://github.com/mctlisboa/rio-v01-validation-20261104/actions/runs/41918223523) passed install, version, doctor, and uninstall on Ubuntu, Alpine, macOS ARM64, and Windows in both PowerShell versions.
- Ten cold and ten warm benchmark runs: cold p50 38.824s/p95 83.377s; warm p50 31.086s/p95 33.566s. Reproduction data and per-check timings are in `docs/benchmarks.md`.
- OpenSpec reports 66/66 tasks complete and validates with zero errors. The user accepted corrected green CI for task 10.3 on 2026-11-05; the original Windows and Ubuntu first-push failures remain recorded in `docs/release-checklist.md`. The final commit records this accepted exception and changes documentation only.

### Stable-release gate

The ten-real-PR evaluation across three repositories and both languages uses **independent automated sub-agent verdicts**, as approved by the user. Its conclusion is **no-go**: 1 useful/9 not-useful reviews, no true positives, substantial diagnostic noise, and two independently reproduced missed regressions. Completeness validation passes, while the stable-release gate correctly rejects this result. This PR does not establish stable-release readiness.

Detailed evidence is in `docs/release-checklist.md`, `docs/release-evidence/`, and `docs/evaluation/v0.1.md`. The RC exists only in the temporary public validation repository; no upstream stable release was published.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added the Rio command-line app for reviewing working-tree, staged, or branch changes, with terminal, JSON, and Markdown reports.
  * Reviews can include TypeScript and Python diagnostics, test coverage, secret detection, dependency compatibility and vulnerability checks, and code-impact summaries.
  * Added profile discovery, validation, and configuration options, plus cache and system diagnostics.
  * Added installers for Linux, macOS, and Windows, with version reporting and uninstall support.
* **Documentation**
  * Added guides for installation, review commands, profiles, adapters, benchmarks, and release evaluation.
